title: Have Blue prototype owned by Lockheed Skunk Works despite Air Force markings
summary: Greg Rogers tells of Have Blue prototype owned by Lockheed Skunk Works despite Air Force markings, about 1970s at Lockheed Skunk Works, and relays what a named person told them. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: when it was uh have blue and it was the preliminary designs, the US Air Force did not own that even though it had US Air Force markings.

plain: Greg Rogers, a doctor who has worked with NASA, says that in the 1970s an experimental aircraft project called Have Blue was not actually owned by the US Air Force, even though the plane carried Air Force markings. As he tells it, it belonged to Skunk Works, the secret design division of the aircraft company Lockheed, while it was still in its early design stage. If true, it would mean private companies can own secret aircraft that look like government property.
